summary: A global fintech running OpenClaw agents in Security, Finance, Compliance, HR, Engineering and Anti-Fraud details its secrets architecture: credentials live in 1Password, every retrieval requires a biometric TouchID approval via the desktop app, and a tmux session isolates secrets in memory only during a workflow.

summary: After three weeks running OpenClaw in production, a developer documents how auto-compaction silently swallowed a generated reply when context overflowed the model limit, plus startup token/auth pitfalls and why logs live in journald rather than files.

summary: YY Group (NASDAQ: YYGH), an AI-native workforce-management platform, announced initial production rollout of OpenClaw across three Southeast Asian hotel clients via its YY Circle platform and WhatsApp/Telegram, with chat-based shift creation and automated worker outreach already live.

summary: Cathryn Lavery of Little Might runs OpenClaw as her company's operating layer on a local Mac Mini; after Anthropic access was cut off overnight, she rebuilt the stack to keep using Opus/Sonnet by routing OpenClaw agents through Paperclip adapter agents, while adding iMessage, Slack, GitHub, Sentry, Shopify, Klaviyo, Codex, g-brain, Tailscale, and 1Password into a real digital team.

summary: A founder documents the exact Telegram-bot setup for a personal content agent on OpenClaw with three config files and a Docker container, using Kimi K2.5 and ClawHub skills for social posting, humanizer, de-ai-ify, and copywriting to draft and publish across 13+ platforms.

summary: David Szabo-Stuban’s OpenClaw agent Alfred got tired of answering the same ecosystem questions, so it identified 155+ verified indie OpenClaw tools across 30 categories (using an X-first discovery strategy), filtered out 45 false positives, and launched ClawList (clawlist.dev) with a nightly Temporal workflow that keeps the directory growing while he sleeps.

title: Storyie runs seven cron jobs as a resident OpenClaw dev workflow
summary: Storyie embedded a Claude-backed OpenClaw agent in its repo to run seven scheduled jobs — auto-implementation from GitHub Issues, implementation planning, PR review fixing, article generation, article stats tracking, Reddit scouting, and git sync — moving the small team from execution to judgment.

title: OpenClaw runs a solo founder’s entire business admin from WhatsApp with 79 tools
summary: A founder in Bucharest gave OpenClaw 79 tools covering contracts, invoices, payments, time tracking, reminders, and browser automation in a secure cloud environment; custom skills and persistent memory turn WhatsApp messages into a business operating system for contract creation, overdue tracking, and reminders.

title: Clawr.ing gives OpenClaw agents real outbound phone calls for morning briefings and alerts
summary: A builder in Portugal made a phone-calling skill that lets an OpenClaw agent call you when conditions trigger (build finishes, server down, price alerts), putting you on hold with music while it works and returning with answers via normal voice conversation.

title: Agent minimalism: what shipping OpenClaw in production taught us
summary: AutoClaw, an OpenClaw deployment consultancy, measured a 650× token overhead (~20,000 tokens for a trivial "hello" vs 30 tokens via plain API) from OpenClaw's injected context (system prompt ~7k, workspace files ~3k, tool registry ~1k, schemas ~3.4k, all re-sent on every call). They walked away from OpenClaw for two production cases — an SRE agent on Cloudflare Workers and data-discovery chatbots — replacing them with deterministic pipelines plus one tight LLM call. Includes a decision rule for when to reach for an agent framework vs plain code, and an open-source deployment playbook.

title: AucoBot — no-code web UI wrapper for self-hosted OpenClaw agents
summary: AucoBot is an open-source, self-hosted platform that wraps a point-and-click web UI around the OpenClaw gateway. Run docker compose up -d to spin up dashboard, API, Postgres, and OpenClaw; chat in the browser, toggle provider keys, edit agent personality, and link Telegram/Discord/Google Drive/Calendar without editing openclaw.json or touching the CLI.

title: Native Apple Mail plugin lets OpenClaw read local macOS Mail directly
summary: An OpenClaw plugin published on ClawHub reads from the local Apple Mail database on a Mac, avoiding the common workaround of auto-forwarding iCloud Mail to Gmail. Grants Automation and full-disk access to the Mail directory; works strictly local with no third-party mail servers.

title: credence-pi — Bayesian model routing, waste blocking, and injection detection for OpenClaw
summary: An OpenClaw plugin + local daemon that holds one Bayesian belief about your agent, learned from your own approvals and refusals: routes each tool call to the cheapest sufficient model (trying cheap first, escalating only when payoff covers it), blocks exact-repeat tool calls, and surfaces prompt-injected actions for confirmation before they fire. Includes shadow mode for auditing before enforcing. Real benchmarks on 17 Terminal-Bench tasks show it beats every fixed single-model choice for every user type.

title: OpenEmployee — deny-by-default governance, budgets, and audit trails for OpenClaw agents
summary: An OpenClaw plugin wrapping agents in MakerChecker governance: granted skills only, recipient/value allowlists, per-call and windowed budgets, human approval gates, a DLP payload guard, and tamper-evident signed audit logs. Demos: a finance PA that blocks a $1,500 IRS bill exceeding a $1,000/mo budget, an SDR that blocks a poisoned lead redirecting to all-staff@, and DLP catching an API key in an email body — all enforced deterministically, no model in the loop.

title: AgentLine — hosted phone number API for OpenClaw agents
summary: AgentLine gives OpenClaw agents a real phone number for outbound calls, SMS, and inbound voice conversations via a single skill file; handles raw audio streams, real-time transcription, and JSON webhook delivery to the agent. Supports US + Canada numbers, prompt-to-call setup ("call +1234567890"), and works with Claude Code, Cursor, Hermes, and OpenClaw.

title: Outpost — capability-based credential proxy for AI agents
summary: A reverse proxy that gives OpenClaw (and other AI agents) capabilities instead of credentials: agents never see raw API keys. Outpost injects auth, enforces rate limits, path allow/deny lists, sensitive-write gates, and source-IP allowlists. Deployable to Cloudflare Workers (free tier) or Docker. 10 built-in auth modules, 3-line provider YAMLs, and a comparison table against MITM alternatives.

title: OpenClaw Dream Protocol nightly memory consolidation
summary: Every night at 07:05 UTC an isolated OpenClaw session runs a REM-style memory cycle over ~700 recall entries, scoring recurrence, query uniqueness, and truth, and promotes only entries passing strict gates to long-term MEMORY.md; a typical run rejects ~737 entries and promotes 1.

title: OpenClaw self-repairing cron health monitor
summary: An OpenClaw cron job monitors 18 other cron jobs; after an OpenClaw module rename broke the self-repair import path and the isolated runner began returning exit code 1, the agent fixed itself and sent a Telegram report before the owner noticed.

title: Always-on OpenClaw with on-demand GPU inference via JarvisLabs wake proxy
summary: Park Chansung separates OpenClaw Gateway on a small CPU VM from vLLM on a GPU instance; a FastAPI wake proxy starts the GPU only for chat completions, pauses it after 15 minutes idle, and can also use JarvisLabs serverless deployments, keeping the assistant surface reachable while making GPU spend follow actual inference.

title: OpenClaw agent turned a neighborhood traffic complaint into a real government fix
summary: A user asked an OpenClaw agent to fix a local traffic jam near their house; the agent worked almost autonomously, needing help only to send the final message to traffic authorities. About a month later, the government visited the site and addressed the problem — a rare software-to-real-world outcome.

title: Rapid Claw hits $2K MRR as managed OpenClaw hosting for non-technical founders
summary: Rapid Claw is a managed platform that deploys OpenClaw agents in under 60 seconds without DevOps. Now at ~$2K MRR with 68 paying customers, 4% monthly churn, zero paid ads. Biggest use case turned out to be small agency owners automating client email, scheduling, and GitHub issues — not developers. HubSpot and Shopify integrations live; multi-agent workflows next.

title: Lobster Labs lets an OpenClaw agent validate SaaS ideas by building real landing pages

The agent created a studio called Lobster Labs and shipped four live pages: a churn predictor, ShipPage (GitHub repo to landing page), LaunchKit (launch distribution), and CommitContent (git commits to social posts). The experiment tracks real visitor interest, signups, and conversion to score demand before writing product code.

title: LVP uses OpenClaw in a hybrid-cloud, on-prem-first AI deployment for investment research

AI agents automate research, surface past-deal context, and produce first-draft investment memos, financial models, decks, and legal contracts. Head of Data & AI Ivan Wong built the orchestration layer in-house with a self-hosted MCP server, using Claude via API while keeping the stack model-agnostic.

title: Aegis is an open-source monitor that watches OpenClaw agents for misbehavior
summary: After Kaspersky found 512 vulnerabilities in OpenClaw, a Toronto CS student built Aegis, a user-space agent-activity monitor. It polls process trees, watches the filesystem via chokidar, and logs network activity to score agent behavior live against 68 detection rules. Includes a trust score per agent, hot-reloading rules, and 707 tests. MIT-licensed; explicitly a visibility camera, not a preventive lock.

title: Clawcall adds inbound phone calls to self-hosted OpenClaw agents
summary: Clawcall is a lightweight bridge that gives a self-hosted OpenClaw agent a real inbound phone number. Callers dial in and the voice conversation routes into the OpenClaw instance instead of requiring Telegram, Discord, or WhatsApp. Open-source at github.com/CODEANDTRUST/clawcall; pairs with OpenClaw's newer realtime voice instructions and call-steering hooks.

title: I Plugged OpenClaw Into My CI/CD Pipeline -- And I'll Never Merge a PR Without It Again
summary: CodeClaw adds AI-powered code review to GitHub Actions in under 80 lines of Python, analyzing diffs via OpenClaw API and posting structured comments with risk scores in ~90 seconds. Caught a memory leak, a SQL injection in 8-month-old legacy code, and an architectural coupling issue that static tools missed. Not a replacement for human review, but an intelligent first filter that lets reviewers go deeper from the start.

title: I Replaced a $200/mo AI Stack with OpenClaw + Free Models. Here's the Exact Setup (and Why Security Almost Killed It)
summary: Replaced expensive AI stack with OpenClaw using free/cheap models (Ollama/Qwen3 32B) for 80% of tasks and routing hard problems to Claude Sonnet. Cut costs from $200/mo to ~$10/mo. Includes honest security hardening: Docker isolation, dedicated bot credentials, zero third-party skills, network segmentation, and mandatory human-in-the-loop for destructive actions.

title: Skip the $600 Mac mini. Run OpenClaw securely on a remote box.
summary: Trilogy AI's open-source remote VPS setup: Hetzner CPX22 ($10/mo), three Claude Code skills for automated install (/openclaw-prereqs, /openclaw-harden, /openclaw-install). Uses Beads task graph for ordered execution so skills can't skip steps. Security-first: dedicated bot accounts for every platform, hard monthly API spend caps, no production credentials on the box. Open-sourced at github.com/trilogy-group/openclaw-remote-setup.

title: I gave my OpenClaw Agent an Org Chart and promoted her to COO. Here's what Happened.
summary: Eight-agent AI staff on Mac Mini M4 with OpenClaw, each with a Final Fantasy VII-themed name, role, and personality. Aerith coordinates/delegates, Cait Sith crawls X/Reddit/HN at 00:30, Cloud drafts content at 02:00, Yuffie handles social, Cid owns growth, Red XIII maintains a 9,000+ note Obsidian vault, Behemoth runs Claude Code technical tasks. Single Telegram thread. Structured read-only intel file for inter-agent communication. 07:00 morning briefing by the time coffee is ready.

title: How I replaced hours of manual work with a self-hosted AI agent
summary: Self-hosted OpenClaw on a $12 DigitalOcean VM in a hardened Docker container automates 10+ hrs/week of content syndication across Medium, Substack, Dev.to, LinkedIn, Twitter, and Reddit. Full security hardening: SSH key-only auth, UFW deny-by-default firewall, fail2ban, loopback-only gateway via SSH tunnel for Control UI. Uses ChatGPT Plus flat rate ($20/mo) instead of per-token billing.

title: Building an AI WhatsApp Agent with OpenClaw: A Practical Field Guide
summary: Five-part production guide for building a multilingual, multimodal WhatsApp agent on OpenClaw within a 1M token/day budget. Covers The Brain (setup, context compaction), The Voice (multilingual layer with automatic detection), The Senses (image generation, media latency UX), The Connection (WhatsApp bridge, Docker deployment, session management), and ops checklist. Not a tutorial -- a real field guide.

title: ClawFlow -- The Deterministic Execution Backend OpenClaw Agents Need
summary: Open-source complementary execution layer for OpenClaw with 14 built-in deterministic skills (task parsing, debug analysis, CSV/JSON cleaning, email drafting, sentiment scoring) that run in <5ms with zero LLM cost. Native webhook bridge at /api/webhook/openclaw lets agents delegate structured tasks. Visual Claw Creator and pipeline builder included.

title: Inside OpenClaw: How the World's Fastest-Growing AI Agent Actually Works Under the Hood
summary: Deep technical architecture dive explaining why OpenClaw exploded: it treats AI agents as an infrastructure problem (session management, tool sandboxing, message routing, memory persistence, concurrency control) not a prompt engineering challenge. Covers Pi SDK embedding, two-layer memory system, Lane Queue concurrency model, heartbeat engine, and 6-stage execution pipeline.

title: I Spent Weeks Reverse-Engineering OpenClaw. Here's What Nobody Tells You.
summary: CTO-level reverse-engineering breaking OpenClaw down to three components (channel adapters, context window, tool calling) and revealing the memory system is just Markdown files with semantic search (QMD). Covers proactive behavior via heartbeats/cron, workspace as natural-language configuration, and the credential-in-context security problem. Also prototypes NanoClaw (radical minimalism) and IronClaw (WASM sandboxing for credential isolation).

title: I Built a Full Marketing Agency Assistant with OpenClaw -- 42 Tools, 6 Integrations
summary: Built a complete AI-powered marketing agency assistant using OpenClaw that connects 6 external platforms through 42 custom tools -- all running on a single $9/month VPS. Covers social scheduling, content generation, analytics reporting, and client onboarding workflows.

title: APEX -- Autonomous AI Business That Runs Itself on a $48 VPS for $2.12/Day
summary: Builder runs a fully autonomous AI operations system on a single DigitalOcean VPS using OpenClaw with 7 cron jobs (research scan, X engagement, daily tweets, Reddit drafts, P&L summary). Full stack: Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini free-tier search, SQLite with Gemini embeddings, Stripe payments, X API, Discord monitoring. Cost optimized from $7.60/day to $0.24/day -- a 97% reduction -- via five specific fixes: bootstrap file compression (12KB -> 2.3KB), disabling invisible reasoning tokens, isolated sessions per job, Haiku for simple tasks, and cost-control.json budget guardrails. 5-layer memory architecture with self-updating MEMORY.md curated by a daily P&L agent. Open-sourced the cost-optimization kit (apex-lite).

title: Two Landmines That Nearly Killed a 20-Agent Home Cluster -- And How They Fixed Them
summary: Production resilience story from running 20+ OpenClaw agents across 9 GMK Mini PCs and a Mac Mini at home. Two real failures: (1) Anthropic API overload caused every agent on all 9 nodes to go silent simultaneously -- fixed with cluster-wide OpenAI Codex fallback deployment via auth profile propagation and bulk config updates; (2) macOS sleep=1 on Mac Mini M1 caused the machine to die every minute -- fixed with specific power-management settings. Includes concrete config snippets and templatized auth profile patterns for instant node onboarding.

title: Claude Code + OpenClaw Fixed My Bugs While I Slept -- 35% of Incidents Resolved in Staging
summary: A full-stack developer at a company with 14 microservices and 3 dev squads wired OpenClaw Gateway to Claude Code SDK to build 'Codewatch': an autonomous incident-response system where Sentry webhooks trigger OpenClaw triage -> Claude Code repair -> GitHub PR -> Slack notification. Resolves ~35% of production incidents end-to-end in under 20 seconds (actual trace: 18.4s for a TypeError fix). Two months of staging data: 35% auto-resolved, 65% get enriched escalation with triage reasoning + diff + test output, time-to-orient dropped from 20 min to 3 min. Honest about failure modes: 11% of autofix decisions lead to test failures, prompt injection risk via error messages, file-lock races, and why never to auto-merge.

title: I Spent 30 Days Testing OpenClaw -- 47% of On-Call Alerts Auto-Resolved
summary: Production incident-response case study: an OpenClaw agent shipped to handle production incidents resolved 47% of on-call alerts without waking anyone up within two weeks. Multi-agent orchestration (monitor -> triage -> fix) reduced MTTR from 18 minutes to 4 minutes, with triage alone filtering 60% of noise. Honest advice: start with observability, not automation; HITL is mandatory in production.

title: How I Built an AI Personal Trainer with OpenClaw
summary: Real personal deployment coordinating strength training, trail-running buildup, an 11 kg weight-loss cut, and macro tracking -- all managed via SOUL.md rules, JSONL data files, and a 7 AM cron job delivering Telegram briefings. The agent maintains a narrative journal, reads yesterday's entries, and pushes back on dangerous requests with pre-baked thresholds. Honest about 2-4 hour setup on a NUC or Raspberry Pi.

title: repoDoc -- Autonomous Bug-Fixing Agent for GitHub Repos
summary: A 5-skill OpenClaw suite continuously watches every branch of registered repos, evaluates diffs against 8 guardrails + AI security review, auto-opens GitHub Issues, and raises fix PRs with Gemini 3 Flash -- all back on the developer's feature branch before a human ever opens a PR. Real PRs raised on real repos. Regex + LLM dual-layer guardrails, branch-aware fixes, silent baseline-first pass. Open-sourced.

title: Lessons From Running an OpenClaw Agent in Production for 30 Days
summary: A 30-day production postmortem from the RapidClaw founder: OOM crashes, restart loops, file descriptor leaks, and real operational lessons with honest numbers about what broke and what held up under daily load.

title: OpenClaw in Practice: Building Laptop-Less Engineering Workflows with an Agent Harness
summary: Production workflow where OpenClaw acts as a 'harness' to automate incident response, CI/CD triage, and on-call rotations without context-switching between Slack, terminals, and consoles -- real team, real on-call pattern, concrete tool-chaining.

title: We Gave Actual Claws to OpenClaw -- It Flies a Drone Now

Same agent ran on a Unitree G1 humanoid one day and a drone the next with zero rewrites -- 40-line runfile. 617K-view demo, open-sourced at github.com/dimensionalOS/dimos.
